<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation
[HALOps](https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/HALOps) is the PaddlePaddle team's high-performance kernel library for NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100). This PR integrates its W8A8 MXFP8 dense GEMM and fused `group_wise_quant` activation quantizer. It also integrates the MXFP8 MegaMoE path used in the benchmark below: MXFP8 experts are served by the existing DeepGEMM MegaMoE W8A8 (`fp8xfp8`) kernel, and the MoE scale layout stays canonical so MegaMoE can derive its own layout from it.

SGLang already serves MXFP8 dense linears through DeepGEMM and FlashInfer. HALOps is added as a third backend, selected explicitly with `--fp8-gemm-backend halops`. Defaults are unchanged: `auto` never resolves to HALOps, and the package is not imported unless the flag is set.

The `halops` wheel is published on PaddlePaddle's CUDA 13.2 package page rather than PyPI and ships cp312/Linux wheels only (x86_64 and aarch64). The official Docker image installs it in a parallel build stage, skipping the package when no wheel matches the build platform; outside Docker, install it with:

```bash
pip install halops==0.1.0 \
  -f https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu132/halops/
```
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Usage

Use the following example to serve DeepSeek-V4-Flash with online MXFP8 quantization and HALOps dense GEMM:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Attention HALOps MXFP8 + MoE MegaMoE MXFP8
set -e

export SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0
export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0
export SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=1
export SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1
export SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_ONLINE_C128_MTP=1

export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096

MODEL_PATH=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-bf16
PORT="${PORT:-30000}"

sglang serve \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --tp 4 \
  --dp 4 \
  --ep 4 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --moe-a2a-backend megamoe \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --quantization mxfp8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --nccl-port 18201 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 2 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3 \
  --context-length 131072 \
  --allow-auto-truncate \
  --enable-cache-report \
  --enable-metrics \
  --fp8-gemm-backend halops
```

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- `layers/quantization/halops_mxfp8.py`: lazy `halops` loader with an install hint, SfAtom scale swizzle, and the load-time weight quantizer.
- `layers/quantization/halops_mxfp8_linear.py`: W8A8 MXFP8 dense linear runner. Shapes HALOps has no tile for, K not 128-aligned, non-bf16/fp16 activations, and non-SM100 devices fall back to FlashInfer CUTLASS using the canonical scale kept on the layer.
- `layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`: `HALOPS` entries in the FP8/MXFP8 backend enums, resolution, and dispatch. Selecting `halops` for a block-FP8 checkpoint raises instead of silently running a different kernel.
- `layers/quantization/fp8.py`: `weight_scale_inv_halops` prepared at load, apply-path wiring, and canonical MXFP8 MoE quantization for MegaMoE.
- `layers/moe/mega_moe.py`: pick the `fp8xfp8` MMA type from E4M3 expert weights, turn UE8M0 scale bytes into fp32, and read K as un-packed (one element per byte) for that type.
- `arg_groups/choices.py`, a `halops` wheel download stage in `docker/Dockerfile` and `docker/Dockerfile.cu134`, and a documentation entry for the new backend.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_halops_mxfp8.py` (CPU): SfAtom layout, arguments passed to HALOps, dtype handling, and the FlashInfer fallback.
## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->
DeepSeek-V4-Flash on GSM8K, full 1314 samples, 5-shot, greedy, `--max-tokens 4096`. The three arms differ only in `--fp8-gemm-backend`; MoE is MXFP8 MegaMoE in all of them.

| arm | `--fp8-gemm-backend` | gsm8k |
|---|---|---:|
| HALOps | `halops` | 0.895 |
| DeepGEMM | `deep_gemm` | 0.897 |
| FlashInfer | `flashinfer_cutlass` | 0.879 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
On 4*SM100 GPU. DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 / attention-DP4 / EP4, EAGLE, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, `--quantization mxfp8`. Attention dense MXFP8 GEMM is the only variable: MoE is MegaMoE in all three arms and the arms differ only in `--fp8-gemm-backend`.

Dataset level (`bench_serving`, 512 random prompts, mean input 1024 / mean output 128, concurrency 128):

| backend | req/s | out tok/s | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **HALOps** | **23.94** | **1576** | **592 ms** | **74.2 ms** |
| DeepGEMM | 20.23 | 1332 | 1212 ms | 81.2 ms |
| FlashInfer | 19.51 | 1285 | 865 ms | 89.2 ms |

> NOTE: The difference is on the host side, not in the kernels. On the same prefill traces all three backends execute the same 8296 kernels:

| prefill, 16384 in | HALOps | DeepGEMM | FlashInfer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPU kernel total | 421.1 ms | 417.3 ms | 424.3 ms |
| of which MXFP8 dense GEMM | 58.5 ms | 56.9 ms | 61.5 ms |
| CPU-op busy | 1528.8 ms | 1812.6 ms | 2956.7 ms |
| CUDA runtime calls | 22,955 | 17,127 | 51,213 |

GPU time is flat within ±2%, so this PR does not claim a GPU-level speedup over the other two backends. HALOps has the lowest CPU-op busy time (breakable CUDA graph not enabled); FlashInfer's host path is the heaviest.

### CPU dispatch overhead

Host dispatch cost vs kernel time at N=8192 / K=4096 on a single GPU, with the benchmark script: [HALOps vs DeepGEMM host-overhead benchmark](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LsvPMVH1KmNcxfKUECui-42uOKnVay9ourd9_BZTxWw/edit).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""HALOps MXFP8 (group-32) dense-GEMM weight helpers.
+
+The load-time half of the HALOps dense GEMM: the optional-package loader, the
+CUTLASS SfAtom 128x4 scale layout, and the online weight quantizer that feeds it.
+"""
+
+from functools import lru_cache
+from typing import Tuple
+
+import torch
+
+HALOPS_MODE = "w8a8-mxfp8"
+
+# HALOps w8a8 needs K % 128 == 0.
+HALOPS_K_ALIGN = 128
+
+# Row alignment of the CUTLASS SfAtom 128x4 scale layout.
+HALOPS_SFATOM_ROW_ALIGN = 128
+
+# HALOps needs M align to 256 when use bias.
+HALOPS_BIAS_M_ALIGN = 256
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def load_halops_gemm():
+    """Return HALOps' ``(dense_gemm, group_wise_quant)``.
+
+    Imported lazily so the wheel is only required once a layer actually needs it,
+    and raises with an install hint rather than a bare ImportError so a
+    ``--fp8-gemm-backend=halops`` run fails at load, not at first token.
+    """
+    try:
+        from halops import dense_gemm, group_wise_quant
+    except ImportError as exc:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "HALOps GEMM backend requested, but the `halops` package is not installed. "
+            "The official Docker image ships it; outside Docker install it with: "
+            "pip install halops==0.1.0 "
+            "-f https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu132/halops/"
+            "or build from source"
+        ) from exc
+    return dense_gemm, group_wise_quant
+
+
+def weight_supported(*, n: int, k: int) -> bool:
+    return k % HALOPS_K_ALIGN == 0 and n % HALOPS_SFATOM_ROW_ALIGN == 0
+
+
+def swizzle_scale_to_sfatom(scale_u8: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Row-major UE8M0 ``[M, K // 32]`` -> the CUTLASS SfAtom 128x4 layout.
+
+    Byte-identical to ``group_wise_quant(use_swizzle=True)`` (verified against it),
+    so a scale that is already quantized still reaches ``dense_gemm``. Needs
+    ``M % 128 == 0`` and ``K % 128 == 0``.
+    """
+    m, k_groups = scale_u8.shape
+    return (
+        scale_u8.contiguous()
+        .view(m // 128, 128, k_groups // 4, 4)
+        .permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
+        .reshape(m // 128, k_groups // 4, 4, 32, 4)
+        .permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)
+        .reshape(m, k_groups)
+        .contiguous()
+    )
+
+
+def quantize_weight(
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Quantize a bf16 ``[N, K]`` weight with HALOps' ``group_wise_quant``.
+
+    Returns ``(fp8 weight, SfAtom scale, row-major scale)``. SfAtom feeds
+    ``dense_gemm``'s ``sfb``; row-major stays in ``weight_scale_inv`` for raw
+    readers and doubles as the FlashInfer fallback scale.
+
+    Requires ``N % 128 == 0`` and ``K % 128 == 0`` -- ``weight_supported`` gates
+    the only caller on exactly that, because the SfAtom 128-row atoms and this
+    swizzle both need it and apply() cannot slice padded output columns.
+
+    One quantization pass: ``use_swizzle=False`` yields the row-major scale, and
+    the SfAtom layout is the same bytes permuted, so swizzle it here rather than
+    asking HALOps to quantize the weight a second time (which would also allocate
+    and throw away a second full fp8 tensor). ``swizzle_scale_to_sfatom`` is
+    verified byte-identical to ``group_wise_quant(use_swizzle=True)``, and feeding
+    either one to ``dense_gemm`` gives bit-identical output.
+    """
+    _, group_wise_quant = load_halops_gemm()
+    if weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+        weight = weight.to(torch.bfloat16)
+    fp8_weight, sf_rowmajor = group_wise_quant(
+        weight.contiguous(), mode=HALOPS_MODE, use_swizzle=False
+    )
+    sf_sfatom = swizzle_scale_to_sfatom(sf_rowmajor.view(torch.uint8))
+    return fp8_weight, sf_sfatom, sf_rowmajor

+class TestOfflineCheckpointScales(CustomTestCase):
+    """Load-time handling of a checkpoint that is already quantized.
+
+    The weights and scales come from disk, so nothing may re-quantize them, and
+    the SfAtom layout must be derived from the scale the checkpoint carries.
+    """
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _layer(*, n, k, scale):
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            weight=torch.nn.Parameter(
+                torch.zeros((n, k), dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn), requires_grad=False
+            ),
+            weight_scale_inv=torch.nn.Parameter(scale, requires_grad=False),
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _method(**attrs):
+        # Bypass __init__: these cases drive the load-time scale prep only.
+        method = Fp8LinearMethod.__new__(Fp8LinearMethod)
+        for name, value in attrs.items():
+            setattr(method, name, value)
+        return method

+        )

+            method._process_mxfp8_linear_weight_scale(layer)

+        # step without recapturing CUDA graphs, so the cached SfAtom bytes must
+        # follow the new scale while staying in the storage the graphs captured.
+        n, k = SF_ATOM_ROWS, 4 * SCALE_GROUP

+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(first.data, _sfatom_reference_k4(scale)))

+class TestOnlineQuantizationBuffers(CustomTestCase):
+    """A BF16 checkpoint quantized at load is requantized on every load."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _method():
+        method = Fp8LinearMethod.__new__(Fp8LinearMethod)
+        method.use_mxfp8 = True
+        method.mxfp8_dense_backend = Mxfp8DenseGemmBackend.HALOPS
+        return method
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _quantized(value, scale_value, *, n, k):
+        scale = torch.full((n, k // SCALE_GROUP), scale_value, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        qweight = torch.full((n, k), value, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        return qweight, swizzle_scale_to_sfatom(scale), scale
+
+    def test_requantization_writes_through_the_captured_buffers(self):
+        """update_weights_from_disk does not recapture CUDA graphs, so a second
+        load must overwrite what the first load handed to dense_gemm."""
+        n, k = SF_ATOM_ROWS, 128
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(
+            weight=torch.nn.Parameter(
+                torch.zeros((n, k), dtype=torch.bfloat16), requires_grad=False
+            ),
+            # First load has no weight_scale_inv yet; the quantizer registers it.
+            register_parameter=lambda name, param: setattr(layer, name, param),
+        )
+        method = self._method()
+
+        with mock.patch.object(halops_mxfp8, "quantize_weight") as quantize_weight:
+            quantize_weight.side_effect = [
+                self._quantized(1.0, 127, n=n, k=k),
+                self._quantized(2.0, 128, n=n, k=k),
+            ]
+            method._quantize_mxfp8_weights(layer)
+            captured = {
+                name: getattr(layer, name).data_ptr()
+                for name in ("weight", "weight_scale_inv", "weight_scale_inv_halops")
+            }
+            method._quantize_mxfp8_weights(layer)
+
+        self.assertEqual(quantize_weight.call_count, 2)
+        for name, data_ptr in captured.items():
+            self.assertEqual(getattr(layer, name).data_ptr(), data_ptr, name)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(layer.weight.data.float(), torch.full((n, k), 2.0)))
+        expected_scale = torch.full((n, k // SCALE_GROUP), 128, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(layer.weight_scale_inv.data, expected_scale))
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(
+                layer.weight_scale_inv_halops.data,
+                swizzle_scale_to_sfatom(expected_scale),
+            )
+        )
+

+    unittest.main()
